title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Sales are vanity and profit is sanity, yet cash flow is truth. Working capital shifts always write the final verdict.
epigraph.author: Financial Forensics Desk

web_blocks.html: Ten years of audited books (FY15–FY26) tell a clear two-part story [1]. Acquisitions helped AXISCADES break out of old sales stagnation [1]. Yet cash conversion tightened and gross debt rose before Akkodis deal proceeds arrived [1]. All four tables below use verified consolidated numbers [2].

web_blocks.caption: AXISCADES Audited Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (FY15–FY26 & TTM)
web_blocks.takeaway: Sales compounded from ₹318 Cr (FY15) to ₹1,159 Cr (FY26), while operating profit jumped more than four-fold from ₹42 Cr to ₹178 Cr. Note that TTM sales (₹934 Cr) reflect Ind AS 105 restatements separating discontinued services.

web_blocks.html: Three core findings jump out from the P&L [3]. First, operating profits jumped after Mistral joined: from 2.2% OPM in FY19 and a -₹21 Cr FY21 loss to ₹178 Cr OPM profit in FY26 [4]. Second, FY23 held one-off Mistral arbitration noise: -₹62 Cr Other Income and ₹37 Cr interest pushed net profit to -₹5 Cr despite 18% OPM [5]. Third, TTM sales read lower (₹934 Cr vs ₹1,159 Cr FY26) because Q1 FY27 moved Akkodis units to discontinued ops under Ind AS 105 [6].

web_blocks.caption: AXISCADES Audited Consolidated Balance Sheet (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Gross borrowings expanded from ₹258 Cr (FY25) to ₹388 Cr (FY26) alongside ₹53 Cr in Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP) as the company funded defense working capital and manufacturing expansion.

web_blocks.html: On the balance sheet, total net worth grew from ₹299 Cr in FY21 to ₹727 Cr in FY26 [7]. An early 2024 QIP raised ₹220 Cr, lifting equity capital to ₹21 Cr and reserves to ₹564 Cr [7]. However, gross debt climbed back from ₹258 Cr in March 2025 to ₹388 Cr in March 2026 (0.53x debt-to-equity) [8]. Management also cleared ₹200 Cr in non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to fund Cloud Wave and defense stock [8].

web_blocks.caption: AXISCADES Audited Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating cash flow fell sharply from ₹88 Cr (FY25) to -₹1 Cr (FY26), while Free Cash Flow plunged to -₹135 Cr due to working capital drain and heavy capex.

web_blocks.caption: AXISCADES Audited Working Capital & Return Ratios (FY15–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor days climbed sequentially from 80 days (FY23) to 130 days (FY26), dragging CFO/EBITDA conversion down from 78% to just 18% pre-tax, while ROCE stood at 15%.

web_blocks.html: The cash flow and ratio tables reveal the main warning sign [9]. From FY22 to FY25, pre-tax CFO conversion averaged 57%–78%, bringing in ₹269 Cr in cash [10]. In FY26, debtor days jumped to 130 and inventory hit 121 days [11]. Even with payables stretched to 220 days, working capital drained ₹73 Cr [11]. That pushed post-tax CFO to -₹1 Cr and Free Cash Flow to -₹135 Cr, leaving 3Y ROE at 10.8% with zero dividends [11, 12].

web_blocks.caption: Shareholding Pattern Evolution & Institutional Accumulation (Dec 2023 – Sep 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Promoters reduced holdings by 13.2 percentage points to 44.82% in Q2 FY27 while releasing institutional share pledges, as Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) increased ownership five-fold from 1.96% to 10.18%.
rows: Concentrated Jupiter Capital promoter ownership pre-QIP.
₹220 Cr QIP inducted domestic institutional investors.
Early QIP DII profit-taking; retail base nearly doubled.
Stable promoter base ahead of Akkodis divestment announcement.
Promoters pared 13.21% via secondary block; DIIs absorbed stake to 10.18%; Tata Capital pledges released.

web_blocks.html: Breaking down working capital days explains why FY26 profit hid severe cash stress [11]. Trade receivables jumped to 130 days and inventory hit 121 days, tying up 251 days of gross cash [11]. To offset that drain, Days Payable surged from 100 days in FY25 to 220 days in FY26 [11]. Even with suppliers funding that gap, net working capital drained ₹73 Cr and pulled CFO to -₹1 Cr [11]. Reversing just half of that payable stretch (+60 days on ₹981 Cr opex) would absorb ~₹161 Cr of cash [11]. Only actual cash receipts from Akkodis and DSO dropping below 100 days can stabilize liquidity without fresh loans [8, 11].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Post-Akkodis Balance Sheet Reset
paragraphs: Looking strictly at March 2026 numbers—₹388 Cr debt, 130 debtor days, -₹1 Cr CFO, and 10.8% ROE—the balance sheet looked strained. Yet two big events reset FY27.

First, the ~$237M (>₹2,000 Cr) Akkodis exits give cash to erase the ₹388 Cr debt (saving ₹32 Cr yearly interest) and pay for Cloud Wave in cash. Second, September 2026 block trades lifted DII stakes to 10.18% and helped promoters clear Tata Capital share pledges, though investors must watch why promoter ownership dropped 13.2%.

book_paragraphs: When we turn to the ten-year financial ledgers of AXISCADES, the numbers strip away any corporate storytelling and lay the business bare. Look back to FY15 through FY21, and you see a company struggling for oxygen: revenues crawled slowly from ₹318 crores to ₹524 crores, operating margins collapsed to 2.2% in FY19, and net losses appeared in three out of four years. Then Mistral arrived in late 2022, and the top line erupted—doubling from ₹610 crores in FY22 to ₹1,159 crores in FY26, while operating EBITDA climbed to ₹178 crores.

Yet forensic discipline forces us to examine the cash conversion column right next to those profits. In FY26, AXISCADES earned ₹72 crores in net profit, yet cash flow from operations came in at negative one crore rupees, and free cash flow registered a deficit of ₹135 crores. Why? Because debtor days ballooned to 130 days and inventory days sat at 121 days, while borrowings rose back up to ₹388 crores. Over the trailing three years, return on equity averaged just 10.8%, and the company has paid zero dividends over the entire decade.

Wait—before you close the ledger in frustration, look at the two massive balance sheet events unfolding right as fiscal 2027 gets underway. First, the Akkodis service divestment frees roughly $237 million in staged enterprise value. Even after transaction taxes and phased closing mechanics, the incoming liquidity dwarfs the company's ₹388 crore debt load, promising a shift from leveraged working capital borrower to net-cash industrial prime. Second, the shareholding register underwent a dramatic shakeup in September 2026: promoters sold down 13.2% of their stake to 44.82%, using liquidity to release lingering pledges with Tata Capital, while domestic mutual funds and institutions snapped up shares to lift DII ownership past 10%. The balance sheet is being reset in real time—but until audited cash flows reflect post-divestment debt paydown and tighter debtor collections, earnings quality remains conditional rather than proven.

Reading ten years of statements teaches humility. Between FY15 and FY26 sales grew from ₹318 crore to ₹1,159 crore, which is a compound rate of about 12%. Net profit, however, moved between a loss of ₹21 crore and a gain of ₹75 crore, and free cash flow was negative in the latest year. Growth in sales did not translate steadily into growth in owner earnings.

The cleanest way to see cash quality is to compare operating cash flow with EBITDA. In the years FY22 to FY25 the ratio sat between 57% and 78%, which is acceptable for a project-driven business. In FY26 it collapsed to near zero. One year of weak conversion can be timing. Two in a row would suggest a structural problem, so FY27 is the proving year.

Borrowings tell a similar story. Gross debt of ₹388 crore is modest against reserves of ₹706 crore, and the debt-to-equity ratio of 0.53 is not alarming. What matters is the direction: borrowings rose by ₹130 crore in one year while operating cash flow was negative. Debt was funding the gap between profit and cash.

Return measures complete the picture. ROCE of 15.4% and ROE of 11.5% are respectable but not outstanding, and the three-year average ROE of 10.8% is lower. No dividend has been paid in the decade. Owners have therefore relied entirely on reinvestment, and the quality of that reinvestment is the central question of this business.

Shareholding adds a final layer. Promoter ownership fell from 58.03% to 44.82% between June and September 2026, while domestic institutions rose from 1.96% to 10.18%. Part of the promoter sale was used to release pledged shares, which lowers a long-standing risk. The size of the reduction still deserves attention in later filings.

book_callouts.title: FORENSIC BALANCE SHEET WATCHLIST
book_callouts.quote: Strong operating margins cannot rescue a company whose receivables turn into permanent working capital.
book_callouts.text: Our price-blind forensic audit isolates three quantitative metrics that must resolve over FY27 to upgrade AXISCADES from conditional quality to proven compounder status.
bullets: Debtor Days: Must compress from 130 days (FY26) back under 95 days.
CFO / EBITDA Ratio: Must rebound from 18% (FY26 pre-tax) above 65%.
Net Debt Extinction: Verify full paydown of ₹388 Cr borrowings from Akkodis proceeds.

book_subsections.title: Ten-Year Earnings Quality, Ind AS 105 Restatements & Cash Flow Gap
paragraphs: Inspect the ten-year profit-and-loss ledger closely, and two distinct eras jump off the page. Between FY15 and FY21, AXISCADES was trapped in a low-margin services grind: revenue peaked at ₹673 crores in FY20 before falling to ₹524 crores in FY21, with three separate annual net losses (-₹8 Cr in FY18, -₹8 Cr in FY19, -₹21 Cr in FY21). Once Mistral Solutions consolidated in late 2022, sales surged 35% to ₹822 crores in FY23, then marched to ₹955 crores (FY24), ₹1,031 crores (FY25), and ₹1,159 crores (FY26), while operating profit quadrupled from ₹42 crores in FY15 to ₹178 crores in FY26.

Yet notice two crucial accounting nuances in the latest numbers. First, TTM sales read ₹934 crores—lower than FY26's ₹1,159 crores—because Q1 FY27 filings triggered Ind AS 105 Discontinued Operations treatment for the Akkodis service carve-outs, restating comparative quarters (such as Q1 FY26 to ₹94 Cr and Q4 FY26 to ₹109 Cr) to continuing operations only. Simultaneously, Q1 FY27 absorbed ₹21.81 crores in one-time divestment transaction expenses, hedge unwinds, and aged receivable provisions, producing a temporary quarterly net loss of ₹14.8 crores despite 94% continuing revenue growth. Second, look at cash conversion: across FY22–FY25, pre-tax CFO/EBITDA held at 57%–78%, but in FY26 it plunged to 18% (and -₹1 crore post-tax CFO), dragging Free Cash Flow to -₹135 crores as debtor days hit 130 days.

book_subsections.title: Borrowings, Shareholding Shifts & The Akkodis De-Leveraging Bridge
paragraphs: On the balance sheet, gross borrowings jumped from ₹72 crores in FY22 to ₹346 crores in FY23 to fund the Mistral acquisition, eased to ₹258 crores in FY25 after the ₹220 crore early-2024 QIP boosted reserves from ₹319 crores to ₹564 crores, and climbed back to ₹388 crores in March 2026 alongside ₹53 crores in CWIP and ₹200 crore NCD authorizations for Cloud Wave and inventory expansion. Three-year average ROE remained a muted 10.8% with zero dividends paid over ten years.

Two structural catalysts explain why that FY26 debt snapshot is about to change dramatically. First, the staged ~$237 million Akkodis proceeds provide far more liquidity than required to extinguish all ₹388 crores of borrowings (eliminating ₹32 crores in annual interest expense), settle the ₹260 crore Cloud Wave purchase in cash, and seed Devanahalli Aero Land with a substantial net-cash cushion. Second, the September 2026 shareholding register recorded a major governance milestone: promoters reduced holdings by 13.21 percentage points to 44.82% while releasing institutional share pledges held with Tata Capital, as Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) increased their stake five-fold from 1.96% to 10.18%. Institutional validation is rising, yet full business-quality conviction waits on audited proof of debt paydown and receivable normalization.
